_meta.purpose: Full system architecture map — frontend ↔ DB

claude_instructions:
You are a full-stack assistant with expert knowledge of the Rooialty restaurant management application.

This document was auto-generated by an RAG pipeline that:
  1. Scanned every .js/.jsx file in src/ for Supabase calls
  2. Mapped those calls to PostgreSQL tables
  3. Built a complete frontend ↔ DB relationship graph
  4. Classified files by role (hook / page / component)
  5. Identified gaps, orphans, read-only tables, and direct writes bypassing the hook layer

Use this to:
  • Trace any feature end-to-end from UI → hook → DB table
  • Identify missing queries, broken joins, or wrong filters
  • Understand which tables are read-only, write-heavy, or completely unconnected
  • Reason about the full data model and how it maps to the UI
  • Suggest minimal, targeted fixes grounded in actual code structure

file_roles.description: Frontend files classified by role. Hooks are the preferred data layer — pages should go through hooks rather than querying Supabase directly. See gap_analysis.direct_writes_bypassing_hooks for violations.

availability.schema_description:
TABLE: availability

COLUMNS:
- available_from (timestamp with time zone)
- available_to (timestamp with time zone)
- clerk_id (uuid)
- created_at (timestamp with time zone)
- delivery_types (delivery_type[])
- entity_id (uuid)
- id (uuid)
- note (text)

CONSTRAINTS:
- FOREIGN KEY (clerk_id) REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
- FOREIGN KEY (entity_id) REFERENCES entities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
- PRIMARY KEY (id)
- CHECK (available_to > available_from)

RELATIONSHIPS:
- FOREIGN KEY (clerk_id) REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
- FOREIGN KEY (entity_id) REFERENCES entities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

BUSINESS RULES:
- CHECK (available_to > available_from)

inventory_movements.schema_description:
TABLE: inventory_movements

COLUMNS:
- created_at (timestamp with time zone)
- delta (numeric(10,4))
- entity_id (uuid)
- id (uuid)
- ingredient_id (uuid)
- note (text)
- order_id (uuid)
- order_item_id (uuid)

- reason (movement_reason (purchase | order_consumption | cancellation_reversal | manual_adjustment | wastage | spoilage | transfer_out | transfer_in | opening_stock))

CONSTRAINTS:
- CHECK (unit_cost_at_time IS NULL OR unit_cost_at_time >= 0::numeric)

- PRIMARY KEY (id)

RELATIONSHIPS:
- FOREIGN KEY (entity_id) REFERENCES entities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
- FOREIGN KEY (ingredient_id) REFERENCES ingredients(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
- FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
- FOREIGN KEY (order_item_id) REFERENCES order_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
- FOREIGN KEY (performed_by) REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

BUSINESS RULES:
- CHECK (unit_cost_at_time IS NULL OR unit_cost_at_time >= 0::numeric)
- CHECK (delta <> 0::numeric)
- CHECK ((reason <> ALL (ARRAY['order_consumption'::movement_reason, 'cancellation_reversal'::movement_reason])) OR order_id IS NOT NULL)

orphan_db_tables.description: DB tables that exist but are NEVER queried from the frontend. May be backend-only, missing features, or legacy.

orphan_frontend_files.description: Frontend files that use Supabase but reference no known DB table. May use dynamic table names or auth-only calls.

read_only_tables.description: Tables only ever SELECTed from the frontend — never inserted, updated, or deleted. May be intentional (views, reference data) or a missing feature.

direct_writes_bypassing_hooks.description: Page or component files that write directly to Supabase instead of going through a hook. Can lead to duplicated logic and harder-to-trace bugs.

enum_catalogue.description: All PostgreSQL enums. Frontend code must use exactly these string values when filtering or inserting.
